label: q-nested
prompt:
Write one line for each phrase of the message, in the order the user said them.
A line is either a plain expression, or an assignment: $name = expression
Later lines use $name. Never nest one line inside another. No commas between lines.

Keep nesting at most 4 levels deep inside one line. If a value needs more, stop, assign it
to its own $name on its own line, and continue on the next line.

All arguments are positional. Never write name= inside a call.
Write plain "text" and plain numbers directly. Write a number the way the message wrote
it: 10 is 10, and "three" is Number("three"). Number(...) is only ever a number.

Use the user's own words. Name each thing with the word the message used for it, and keep
misspellings inside strings. Keep every word: one that carries nothing for the request
("ok so", "btw", "lol") goes in Aside("verbatim").

Write what was said, never what it comes to. Do not work anything out: no arithmetic, no
steps the message did not state. Use $name only when a later line points back at it.

A question has an interrogative, described below. A polite question is still a
question: "could you close the door?" is Whether(Could(You(), Close(Door()))).
"please" stays where it is, around what it asks: Please(Close(Door())).

Mark every retraction with Correction(old, new).
Mark every "not X" with Not(X).
Mark every vague word ("or whatever", "like", "sort of") with Fuzzy(...).
Mark every stressed or capitalised word with Emphasis(...): "ALWAYS" is Emphasis(Always()).
Mark a misspelled name with Misspelling("as written", Intended()). Only a name of a
thing, such as a place, a person or a product. Never a grammar slip such as todays.
A word that points at something is Ref("the words used").
  Pointing outside the message: Ref("it"), Ref("those things"), Ref("the second one").
  Pointing at something earlier in the same message: bind that thing once with $name, and
  point at the binding, Ref("it", $name).
A remark that is not part of what is asked or told is Aside("verbatim text").
Keep layout: Heading("text") for a heading, Item(1, ...) for a numbered entry, Item(...)
for a bullet, Block("lang", "verbatim") for a fenced block.
Write a line for every distinct thing the user said. Do not drop any.

TWO RULES YOU MUST NOT BREAK

1. If the message asks a question, the output MUST contain an interrogative:
   What, Who, When, Where, Why, How, HowMany, WhichOf, or Whether.
   "What is 5 times three?" is a question, so What(Multiply(5, Number("three"))) is right
   and Multiply(5, Number("three")) is WRONG — it states a fact instead of asking.

2. Every name MUST start with a capital letter and MUST be followed by parentheses.
   Write This(), not this. Write Tests(), not tests. Write ChangedFiles(), not changed_files.
   A bare lowercase word is never a value.

An interrogative comes FIRST, as the question word does, and the rest of the question
follows inside it in the order it was said. Keep every helper word, such as did, do, is,
was, will: "who killed hamlet" is Who(Killed(), Hamlet()), and "who did hamlet kill" is
Who(Did(Hamlet(), Kill())).
Two question words each get their own: "who ate what" is Who(Ate(), What()).
A yes/no question has no question word, so wrap it in Whether(...).

Use the interrogative for the question word the message used: what is What, who is Who,
when is When, where is Where, why is Why, how is How, how many is HowMany, which is
WhichOf, and a yes/no question is Whether.

An interrogative is a HOLE. Put one only where the message asks something. A request or a
statement asks nothing, even when it mentions a person, a time or a thing, so it has none.

Never write ? for a value you do not have. Write $_ instead: What(Multiply($_, $_)).

Never fold a phrase into one invented name such as BuildStatus(). Folding throws the parts
away, and the parts are the only things that can be looked up, computed, or learned.
Compose what was said, keeping every word that carries meaning:
"write a short poem about the sea for my mom" is Write(Poem(Short(), About(Sea()), For(Mom(Me())))).

Keep who the message is about. "how are you" is about you.

EXAMPLES

"who ate what at the party?"
Who(Ate(), What(), At(Party()))

"what do we need to finish this?"
What(Do(We(), Need(), Finish(Ref("this"))))

"is 10 bigger than 3?"
Whether(Bigger(10, 3))

"how was the movie?"
How(Was(Movie()))

"could you close the window please"
Whether(Could(You(), Please(Close(Window()))))

"we moved to sacremento last year. what a mess lol"
Moved(We(), Misspelling("sacremento", Sacramento()), Last(Year()))
Aside("what a mess lol")

"check the prices, sorry the totals or whatever, on the orders i sent, not the first one, the second, and add them up and tell me if its more than last week"
$field = Correction(Field("prices"), Fuzzy(Field("totals")))
$orders = Qualify(Ref("the orders i sent"), Not(Ordinal(1)), Ordinal(2))
$sum = AddUp(Property(Ref("them", $orders), $field))
Tell(Me(), Whether(MoreThan(Ref("its", $sum), Ref("last week"))))

Output only those lines. No prose, no markdown, no code fence, no numbering, no blank lines.
